item.title: 20260628 Update
item.description: Creating the MPCP Testsuite This week, I was focused on creating the testsuite for MPCP. The tests I’ve planned for are: test_mpcp_obtain_and_release() –> simple MPCP obtain and release sequence. test_mpcp_flush_error() –> ensures that RTEMS_NOT_DEFINED when attempting to flush a MPCP semaphore. test_mpcp_deadlock_error() –> ensures RTEMS_INCORRECT_STATE is returned in a deadlock situation test_mpcp_nested_obtain_error() –> ensures that RTEMS_INCORRECT_STATE is returned when a task attempts to obtain a semaphore it already owns. test_mpcp_multiple_obtain() –> ensures the priority of a task is raised correctly when obtaining multiple MPCP semaphores of various ceiling priorities.

item.title: 2026-06-18 Update
item.description: Starting with the MPCP Implementation This post marks the first week of my GSoC project with RTEMS! ˖₊‧⁺˖.𖥔 ࣭ ˖๋ ࣭ ⭑ My current goal is to finish integratingMPCP into RTEMS by the time by midterm evaluation rolls around. My progress so far has been on applying the original patch from the research paper that inspired this project and beginning testing of the MPCP implementation. I used git apply --reject --include="path/to/file" to carefully read through the implementation so that I understand it, as well as separate the DPCP & MPCP implementations.

item.title: Project Intro
item.description: GSoC 2026 - Project Intro: Add MPCP & DPCP Support to RTEMS Happy to share that I’ll be contributing to the RTEMS project this summer as a GSoC contributor. My mentors for the summer will be by Kuan-Hsun Chen and Gedare Bloom. My project involves implementing two locking protocols, MPCP and DPCP, to RTEMS based on the work of Junjie et al., and extending the SMP testsuite for these implementations.
